strings.name: Carlos Tavares
strings.role: Portuguese automotive executive and former Stellantis CEO
strings.summary: Carlos Tavares held management roles at Renault, Nissan and PSA, helped consolidate Europe's automotive industry and became Stellantis's first CEO. He resigned on December 1, 2024; his career encompasses corporate restructuring and departure following disagreements with the board.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026; evidence of living status is an interview published August 17. Former titles are retained, and transaction closing, governance effectiveness and succession dates distinguished. Industry-policy comments are attributed to him.
strings.influence.rationale: Led PSA's recovery and helped create Stellantis, influencing consolidation in Europe's automotive industry.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated from École Centrale Paris in 1981 with an engineering education.
strings.facts.f2.label: Leadership transition
strings.facts.f2.value: After his December 2024 departure, John Elkann led an interim executive committee; Antonio Filosa became CEO on June 23, 2025.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Integration across companies
strings.highlights.h1.text: From PSA's purchase of Opel and Vauxhall to its merger with FCA to create Stellantis, he participated in integrating multiple brands; transactions and operating results reflect the work of many parties.
strings.highlights.h2.title: End of tenure and industry reflections
strings.highlights.h2.text: The company attributed his 2024 departure to differing views; in a 2026 interview he criticized European automotive policy. These assessments represent his personal position.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Interview after retirement
strings.timeline.t1.text: Executive Digest published an interview conducted in Portugal about automotive competition and regulation; publication and interview dates are not necessarily the same.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Resigned as Stellantis CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: The board accepted his resignation with immediate effect and an interim executive committee took over; he did not remain until the previously planned 2026 departure.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became Stellantis's first CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: The PSA–FCA merger closed the previous day; the new name and governance took effect on January 17, with him as CEO and executive director.
strings.timeline.t4.title: PSA completed its Opel and Vauxhall acquisition
strings.timeline.t4.text: The automotive business passed from General Motors to PSA; European financing operations were a separate transaction still being pursued.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became chairman of PSA's Managing Board
strings.timeline.t5.text: He first joined the Managing Board on January 1 and became chairman at the end of March; this body is distinct from the Supervisory Board.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Led Nissan's Americas operations
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became executive vice president, chairman of the Americas Management Committee and president of Nissan North America, rather than Nissan's global CEO.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Moved to Nissan
strings.timeline.t7.text: After his long service at Renault, he took management roles at its alliance partner Nissan.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined Renault
strings.timeline.t8.text: With an engineering background, he began his automotive career at Renault.
